scene1_screen1.text: These days, Anna worked alone. No badge. No agency. Just instincts, grudges, and leads she paid for in favors. Tonight’s trail ended here — a luxury hotel with too many cameras and one too-perfect tip.

scene1_screen3.text: The message was simple: Room 313. Midnight. You’ll find what you’ve been chasing. No signature. But Anna knew who it pointed to. And she was done waiting.

scene1_screen4.text: The keycard flickered — red, then green. She pushed the door open.

scene1_screen6.text: She steps in. Kicks off her heels. Reaches for the light switch — and freezes.

scene1_screen7.text: There’s someone in the room. A man, slumped against the wall, shirt soaked in blood. Breathing. Watching.

scene1_screen8.text: And beyond him — sprawled by the bed — a second figure. Motionless. Face down. A pool of blood already congealing beneath the head.

scene1_screen11.text: (hoarse, low) Rivera. Huh. You weren’t on the guest list.

scene1_screen12.text: (flat) Last I heard, you were desk-bound in Munich.

scene1_screen13.text: And you were too clean for field ops. Guess we both disappointed someone.

scene1_screen14.text: He doesn’t move. Doesn’t reach for anything. But his posture is coiled. Strained. Like he’s bracing for a fight — or the end.

scene1_screen17.text: He shifts, barely. One hand pressed to his side. She spots an open suitcase on the bed. A gun next to it. Untouched. A body? No. Not that she can see. But there’s blood. Too much blood for someone to walk away.

scene1_screen19.text: (strained) Got a lead. Came alone. Walked in. Found blood, no source. Door shut behind me. Then the pain started.

scene1_screen20.text: She kneels beside him. Her hands are quick — trained. She rips a strip from the bedsheet and starts wrapping it around his torso.

scene1_screen21.text: Still as efficient as they say.

scene1_screen22.text: She doesn’t answer, but her eyes flick to his chest — cut, scarred, solid. Her fingers hesitate for half a second.

scene1_screen23.text: (noticing) Careful. That look says you missed me. Or maybe you're just admiring the damage. I don’t mind.

scene1_screen25.text: (dryly) You’re lucky I still remember where to apply pressure.

opts.text: Check other rooms in the suite.
Push him for a detailed explanation.
Leave him — this wasn’t part of your mission.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Anna stands silently, gaze drifting toward the inner hallway of the suite. She moves, controlled but swift, past the minibar and into the shadows. James tries to sit up, but she shoots him a look.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Stay down. Bleeding all over the carpet’s enough of a statement.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: The first door leads to the bathroom — empty. The second creaks as she opens it. A smaller guest room. Clean, mostly — except for the faint scent of smoke… and a still-warm cup of coffee on the nightstand.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen5.text: She steps back into the main room, eyes sharper, voice lower.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Either you were bait… or someone wanted us both in this room.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen8.text: Only if the next thing I find isn’t a body.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Anna doesn’t move. Instead, she kneels beside the bed, not touching him, but close enough to see the tension behind his eyes.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Start from the beginning. No riddles, no half-truths. Why are you here?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: I got a message. No sender, just a time, a room number… and a promise.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen5.text: (quiet) That I’d find proof. That I could clear my name. Wipe what happened in London two years ago off the books.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen6.text: Her expression flickers — recognition. That op haunts them both.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen7.text: You think ghosts from London come with room service now?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen8.text: I didn’t expect you to walk through the door. That part wasn’t in the plan.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen9.text: She leans back slightly, eyes never leaving his.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen10.text: No. But it might be the only reason you’re not dead yet.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Anna rises slowly. Methodical. Cold. She checks the door, her hand already on the knob.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: I came for intel. Not for buried mistakes bleeding on hotel floors.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: She pauses, not turning around, and narrows her eyes — not sure if it’s a compliment or a warning.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen5.text: You should be glad I showed up. Whoever sent that message didn’t plan on you walking out of here.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen7.text: She hesitates. Just long enough for doubt to slip in. Then — she exhales through her nose and steps away from the door, annoyed at herself.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen8.text: Don’t mistake this for kindness. I just hate loose ends.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen9.text: But they both know that’s not the only reason.

scene1_screen26.text: Outside, hotel life rolls on: elevator dings, laughter from the bar, footsteps down the hall.

scene1_screen27.text: But inside Room 313? The trap was already closing.

scene2_screen1.text: For a few seconds, neither of them speaks. Anna stands near the door. James sits against the wall, one arm still pressed to his side. The silence is thick — with tension, with doubt, with something they haven’t named yet.

scene2_screen2.text: (quietly) I was looking for someone. A man. His name’s Piers Lark.

scene2_screen3.text: The moment she says it, James straightens. The name hits like a bullet.

scene2_screen4.text: Lark. He was my lead. Supposed to meet him tonight.

scene2_screen5.text: (sharp) And now your contact’s dead. In your hotel room.

scene2_screen6.text: (bitter) And whoever arranged this wanted both of us tangled in it.

scene2_screen7.text: Her expression tightens. She’s piecing it together just as fast as he is.

scene2_screen9.text: James nods — slowly. His breath shallow, but his mind clearer than it’s been all night.

scene2_screen10.text: And whoever did it isn’t finished.

scene2_screen11.text: A noise echoes outside the door. Soft. Deliberate. Like someone trying not to be heard.

scene2_screen14.text: She moves quickly, helping him to his feet. He grunts but manages to stand, leaning on her. Her arm wraps around his back. Not for comfort — not entirely. She’s steadier than he remembers.

scene2_screen15.text: The shadows beyond the hallway flicker with movement.

opts.text: Hide in the closet and listen.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: James nods toward the closet. They move quickly — but silently. He slips in first. Anna follows, closing the door behind them. Inside: pitch black. Heartbeats loud. Breath held.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Footsteps. Slow. Measured. Someone walks the room. A flashlight beam cuts through the space — flicking over the bed, the suitcase, the floor.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (muttering) No body. No trace. He’s gone?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: The light lands briefly on Anna’s heel beneath the closet door — then shifts away. It lingers a second too long. James barely breathes.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen6.text: Silence. Then retreating steps. The door closes. A long beat. Stillness.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen7.text: They step out of the closet. The room is undisturbed — but the air feels thinner. The rules of the game just changed.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen9.text: Then let’s give him a reason to regret it.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: James jerks his chin toward the balcony door.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Fire escape. If we’re lucky, it leads down near the service level.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Anna helps him to the balcony. She listens. Quiet. Then eases the door open.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: They climb over the railing onto a narrow fire escape. Below — shadowy alleys and the hum of the hotel’s industrial units. Step by step, they descend the shaky metal stairs.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen5.text: At the second floor, a window stands slightly ajar — unmarked, dusty. She nudges it open with her foot.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen6.text: They slip inside and find themselves in a cluttered storage room. Crates, linens, staff equipment. A service map pinned to the wall.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen7.text: Anna spots a door marked “Maintenance Access” and opens it into a dim corridor — concrete, exposed wiring, flickering lights.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen8.text: Behind them, soft voices rise outside — not police. Not staff. Too calm. Too purposeful.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen9.text: (urgent) They’re tracking our route. Keep left. Always left.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen10.text: They pick up the pace, vanishing into the maze of service tunnels.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: James grabs the gun from the bed. Anna gets hers too.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen3.text: He swings the door open fast — just as a man in hotel uniform raises his hand toward the handle. But his eyes aren’t the eyes of a bellhop. They’re focused. Wrong.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Anna doesn’t hesitate. Elbow, throat, wall. Three moves. He’s out cold before he registers the threat.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen7.text: They leave the room in a hurry. No more guessing. No more hiding. They move — fast, together — and vanish into the night.

scene3_screen1.text: They emerge into the night air — sharp, biting, real. Behind them: an unknown person in the corridor, a corpse in Room 313. Ahead: nothing but rooftop silence and ten uncertain minutes.

scene3_screen2.text: Anna moves first. She scans the corners, then pulls a burner phone from the inner lining of her jacket. No hesitation. No delay. Her fingers fly across the screen with encrypted precision.

scene3_screen3.text: (watching her) That’s not a standard-issue hotel phone.

scene3_screen4.text: (without looking up) Neither’s the man bleeding next to a dead body.

scene3_screen5.text: James almost smiles. Almost. But there’s too much weight in the air.

scene3_screen6.text: (after a beat) So what now? Call for help that doesn’t exist?

scene3_screen7.text: (cold) No one’s coming. Lark made sure of that. And if we don’t find him first, we’re dead before sunrise.

scene3_screen8.text: The wind tugs at her hair. Her focus never wavers. But something flickers beneath the surface — just for a second.

scene3_screen9.text: He made it personal, didn’t he?

scene3_screen11.text: (softly) He always does. He leaves just enough evidence to ruin you, just enough silence to isolate you.

scene3_screen12.text: James steps closer, not crowding her — but there. Solid. Grounded.

scene3_screen13.text: (gently) He framed me. Killed a man in my room. But I get the feeling… this goes deeper for you.

scene3_screen15.text: (after a pause) Three years ago. He torched a safe house. My partner was inside. Lark made it look like she blew the mission. Left a note. They buried her with her reputation in shreds.

scene3_screen16.text: (quiet) And you’ve been chasing him ever since?

scene3_screen18.text: She exhales — like the truth cost her breath. Then finally looks at him.

scene3_screen19.text: And you? You knew Lark by name.

scene3_screen20.text: (sighing) I thought I was getting a second chance. Not redemption — just a shot at truth. They erased everything after London. I’ve been a shadow with a badge ever since.

scene3_screen21.text: (softer) So you walked in blind, hoping to fix what they broke.

scene3_screen22.text: No backup. No exit. Just a room number and a lie I wanted to believe.

scene3_screen23.text: His voice doesn’t shake. But there’s something raw beneath it — not weakness, just the cost of still caring.

scene3_screen24.text: Anna studies him for a long moment.

scene3_screen25.text: (soft) You always took the weight of the world like it owed you something.

scene3_screen26.text: (wry) Better than pretending none of it mattered.

scene3_screen27.text: A breeze cuts through again. This time they both feel it — that pulse between them. It’s not fear. It’s recognition. Tension. Something that’s been building since the moment she walked through the wrong door. Or maybe earlier?

scene3_choice1.text: What do you do with this moment?

opts.text: Stay close — but keep the line.
Pull away — now’s not the time.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She doesn’t speak — just lets her body shift slightly toward his. Close, but not clinging. It’s not about comfort. It’s about grounding.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: James shifts slightly, turning to face her more fully. The rooftop wind tousles her hair. His expression softens — not with charm, but recognition.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (quiet) When you walked into that room… for a second, I thought I was hallucinating.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen5.text: (genuine) Relieved. Which probably means I’ve lost my edge.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen6.text: She doesn’t laugh — but there’s the shadow of a smile. Faint. Real.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen7.text: I’ve been in worse situations. But I don’t remember feeling this… unarmed.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen9.text: Her fingers tighten in his. Not much. But enough. The cold air doesn’t touch them now.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen10.text: We get out of this… maybe I’ll let you buy the first round.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen11.text: Deal. Just don’t vanish before then.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen12.text: She leans her head briefly against his shoulder — not weakness, not romance. Something older. Quieter. A beginning, maybe.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen14.text: They stay like that a beat longer. Still tense. Still hunted. But not alone anymore.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She lets their fingers remain intertwined — but draws the line there.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (quiet) We make it through this… maybe we talk about what this is. But right now — it’s him or us.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Still, his thumb brushes lightly against hers. A small act. Measured. Not asking for more — just letting her know he’s there.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen5.text: You always this calm before chaos?

scene3_choice1_option2_screen7.text: She smiles. Briefly. Not flirty. Just real. They both look back toward the stairwell — the world still burning behind them.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: She lets go of his hand. Not with anger. Not rejection. Just clarity.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: We’re not here for this. We’re here because someone wanted us out of the picture.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: James holds her gaze — searching for something. Then nods, once. No pushback.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen5.text: But there’s something in his eyes — not disappointment, but memory. Of the rooftop. Of what almost was.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen6.text: (flat) Let’s move. Before Lark decides to finish what he started.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen7.text: No lingering. No indulgence. Just two agents stepping back into the fire.

scene3_screen29.text: A phone buzzes softly. Signal found. Anna looks down, then up.

scene3_screen30.text: (sharp) That signal we planted? Lark just pinged it. Must’ve taken the bait.

scene3_screen32.text: (curt) I embedded a tracker in the decoy drive — the one the contact was supposed to deliver. Lark couldn’t resist checking it. Now we know where he is.

scene3_screen33.text: James nods once. Impressed. Resigned. Ready.

scene3_screen35.text: They disappear back into the hotel’s maze — not alone, not anymore. Two ghosts chasing the devil, who tried to bury them.

scene4_screen1.text: They follow the location trace Anna dropped into Lark’s private channel. A dead signal pinged to a locked utility wing — disused, hidden from the hotel’s main blueprints. Exactly the kind of place Lark would pick for a message... or an ambush.

scene4_screen2.text: James scans the hallway. His instincts prickle. He’s seen these setups before — as a handler, in deep cover, years ago.

scene4_screen3.text: (low, alert) It’s too quiet. Too easy.

scene4_screen4.text: He’s not just sending a message. He wants a stage.

scene4_screen5.text: (focused) That’s fine. Let’s give him an audience.

scene4_screen6.text: Anna breaks the lock with a flick of her wrist and steps into the corridor.

scene4_screen7.text: The air is stale. The plaster cracked. No cameras. No motion sensors. Just silence.

scene4_screen8.text: (behind her) I don’t like this. It’s too—

scene4_screen10.text: Her voice is even, but James catches the shift in her tone — the edge of something personal, bitter. She pushes forward with a gun at her side.

scene4_screen11.text: They reach a heavy, metal-plated door left slightly ajar. A soft electronic glow pulses inside.

scene4_screen12.text: (low) He’s expecting me alone. If you follow — he might vanish again. This is his theatre. Cover me.

scene4_screen13.text: Her voice is firm, but James catches the edge of worry beneath it. She steps in alone.

scene4_screen14.text: Anna sweeps the room — gun raised, breath steady.

scene4_screen16.text: No answer. She moves toward the desk — warily.

scene4_screen17.text: On the screen — a live security feed. The entrance. A woman in black blazer. Anna freezes. It’s her — from fifteen minutes ago.

scene4_screen18.text: (under her breath) He’s been watching since the lobby.

scene4_screen19.text: A soft chime. A second monitor flickers. Another view — Room 313.

scene4_screen21.text: She turns to leave. The door slams shut behind her. Automatic lock.

scene4_screen23.text: Then — a hiss. Thin white gas sprays from a vent above.

scene4_screen24.text: (coughing) Son of a…I recognize that smell! It’s not fatal. It’s neuro-inhibitor grade. Disorientation. Short-term paralysis. He used this on her handler once.

scene4_screen25.text: She stumbles toward the desk — hits a button. Nothing. Her limbs shake.

scene4_screen26.text: James hears it. The slam. The hiss. The silence.

scene4_screen30.text: He doesn’t hesitate. Drops to one knee, pulls a thin tool from his belt — tension, twist. The lock resists. One second. Two. Then click — it gives.

scene4_screen31.text: He pushes the heavy metal door open just enough. Hinges groan in protest, but it moves.

scene4_screen32.text: Smoke. Dim light. Anna collapsed near the monitors, still conscious but barely.

scene4_screen34.text: He pulls her up — arm around her, breath ragged.

scene4_screen35.text: (slurred) He knew I’d come alone… baited it…

scene4_screen36.text: (jaw clenched) I’m not letting him win.

scene4_screen37.text: He hoists her into his arms and stumbles out of the gas-filled room. Anna gasps, eyes fluttering open as the cold water soaks them both.

opts.text: Take her to a safe extra room.
Keep her grounded — show her she’s not alone.
Push the emotion down — stay focused.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: He doesn’t stop moving until they’re back in one of the guest rooms — his room. He lays her gently on the bed, wet hair clinging to her cheek.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen5.text: I thought it might come in handy.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen6.text: He wipes water from her face. His hands tremble — not from panic. From fury. From almost losing her.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (hoarse) Next time, you don’t go in alone. Not while I’m here.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen9.text: (bitter) I didn’t know I did either. Until now.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen10.text: He leans down, kisses her forehead. His hand brushes gently along her jaw. His hand lingers at her jaw — steady, gentle.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen11.text: Thank you. For coming for me.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen12.text: She reaches up, fingers touching his wrist — a quiet gesture, but full of meaning.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen14.text: Now we go finish what he started.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen1.text: He helps her sit against the wall. Offers a bottle of water from his go-bag.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen2.text: The smoke has dissipated and the effect is wearing off.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen3.text: (gently) You scared the hell out of me.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: He brushes damp hair behind her ear — a simple gesture. Grounding. Intimate in its restraint.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen6.text: He wants to break you. He didn’t.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen7.text: She exhales shakily — lets her head rest briefly on his shoulder.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen9.text: Then we see it through. You and me.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: He props her against the hallway wall and kneels beside her.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (firm) He knew your pattern. Your instincts. He studied you. Which means he made a mistake.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Because now I’m in the game.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen5.text: He pulls the tablet from the gas room. Rewinds the feed.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Let’s find the detail he didn’t mean to show us.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen7.text: Their hands move in sync over the screen. All the emotion — the fear, the relief — shoved into a box.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen8.text: There’s no time for anything else now.

scene4_screen38.text: Somewhere in the hotel, Lark watches. He knows they’re alive. But now he’s not sure what they’ll do next.

scene4_screen39.text: And that’s the mistake that will cost him.

scene5_screen1.text: The feed from the tablet led them here — into the forgotten upper echelon of the hotel. A place where power once lived. Decisions were made here. Now it reeks of endings.

scene5_screen2.text: James moves quietly, flashlight slicing through the dark. Anna walks beside him, steady again, each step cautious but certain.

scene5_screen5.text: At the far end of the ruined suite: a raised platform, an old projector flickering static onto a cracked wall. And standing before it — Piers Lark, arms folded, eyes cold. Alive with calculation.

scene5_screen6.text: Impeccably dressed. Calm. A ghost in a suit. The man who turned their agency against them

scene5_screen7.text: (mocking) What a stage for a finale. Anna — the orphaned apprentice turned vigilante. James — the good soldier who forgot to lie down. You made it further than I thought. But not far enough.

scene5_screen8.text: James stiffens, jaw tight. But it’s Anna who speaks, voice controlled, razor-sharp.

scene5_screen9.text: Lark nods once. Somewhere in the dark, there’s a faint click. The doors behind them lock. Metal. Final.

scene5_screen10.text: A distant rumble starts — and a red digital counter lights up near the projector: 00:10:00.

scene5_screen12.text: (low, dangerous) Of course I was. I built this game. Every step you took, I let you. Just to see how far you’d crawl before begging. That countdown? Insurance. When it hits zero, all the data goes public. Real names. Real agents. Real blood.

scene5_screen13.text: You killed my handler. Made her death look like cowardice. You framed James, left him for dead in a corridor. Burned everything. Why?

scene5_screen14.text: (shrugging) Because you were liabilities. You care too much. Ask too many questions. And worst of all — you don’t compromise.

scene5_screen15.text: He steps toward the long table, slowly, deliberately — then places a single gun on its surface.

scene5_screen16.text: Behind him, a sealed server tower hums with power, cabled into the projector — the source of the leak.

scene5_screen17.text: So here’s your test. One bullet. One clean shot. You want justice? Revenge? Survival?

scene5_screen18.text: (leaning in) Or maybe you’re just like me — pretending it matters which mask you wear.

scene5_screen19.text: He steps back, arms open — daring them.

scene5_screen20.text: You wanted to be more than pawns. Well, here’s the board. Make your move.

scene5_screen21.text: Anna and James exchange a look. They don’t need to speak.

opts.text: Walk away — and take it all with you

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Anna steps forward, and picks up the gun. Lark’s smirk falters for half a second — a crack in the armor.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (mocking) You think this makes you better than me?

scene5_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (quiet) This isn’t about being better. It’s about stopping you from poisoning what’s left.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen4.text: She fires. The shot is clean. No hesitation. Lark stumbles back, hand pressed to his chest — not surprised, but… insulted.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen5.text: (fading) You… never saw the whole board…

scene5_choice1_option1_screen6.text: He collapses. A legacy written in betrayal — and ended in silence. James exhales beside her. The air shifts — not lighter, just… changed.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (low) We’ll never get medals for this.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen8.text: (without looking away) We don’t need them.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen9.text: She tosses the weapon on the table. James darts to the edge of the table, pulling open the control panel beneath the projector.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen11.text: He yanks the main power cord from the server. The timer freezes at 00:03:04. Freedom, and prevention — bought at a price.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen12.text: A second click. This time — the doors unlatch. Freedom, bought at a price. They walk out without another word.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Anna reaches for the gun — then stops. Slowly offers it to James.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Your name. Your frame-up. Your call.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen3.text: James looks at the weapon for a long moment. Symbol, threat, truth. Lark meets his eyes, and for the first time, there’s a flicker of doubt.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen4.text: You don’t get an easy end. You rot. You watch the empire burn.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen5.text: He lowers the gun, pulls out the data drive — everything Lark tried to hide. Tosses it on the table like a gavel.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen6.text: Everything you buried? The world’s going to know. All of it.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen7.text: And you’ll live just long enough to watch it unravel.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen8.text: Anna steps forward, cuffs Lark to the rusted railing. He watches them with coiled rage, but says nothing… until they reach the exit panel.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen10.text: James opens a locked side panel on the projector unit, exposing manual controls. He flips a heavy switch — the same faint clack sounds behind them: the door unlocking.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen11.text: He yanks out the primary cable to the server, freezing the leak at 6:02. Data preserved. Public exposure prevented.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen12.text: (calling out, voice sharp) You think this is over? You don’t end men like me — we resurface.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen13.text: (without turning) Then next time, we bury you deeper.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen14.text: (quiet) If there is a next time.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen15.text: They walk out into the hallway — not victorious, but clear-eyed. Behind them, the static buzzes, the flickering light casting long shadows over a man still plotting.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Anna stares at Lark. No gun. No anger now. Just absolute clarity.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (cold) You don’t deserve a legacy. So we’re taking that too.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen3.text: She moves to the projector console. Not for violence — for deletion. Hard drives click as she begins wiping them, one by one. James joins her, yanking cables, tossing corrupted cores onto the table.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen4.text: No names. No blackmail. No threats. You vanish.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen5.text: Behind them, the countdown glitches, confused — a self-destructing threat. If nothing survives, there’s nothing to leak.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen6.text: (furious) You fools. You think this ends anything? I have contingencies. Mirrors of mirrors.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen7.text: (turning slightly) We know. We’re erasing those too.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen8.text: She rips open a panel under the desk — finds the power routing node and security override. The words blink red: Locks Engaged. She rewires it with bare fingers, grimacing at the spark.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen9.text: A loud clunk echoes through the ceiling — the final lock disengaging.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen10.text: (desperate, shouting) They’ll never believe you. You’re nothing without me.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen12.text: They tie him to a broken chair with stripped cable. No theatrics — just finality.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen13.text: As they step out into the hallway, the last backup server emits a high whine and dies. Behind them — only silence, and a man left alone with nothing but his ruined ego.

scene6_screen1.text: Room 313 is quiet now. No sirens. No tension. Just the hum of a city that never knew what happened above it.

scene6_screen2.text: One sealed envelope on the nightstand. Inside: Names. Coordinates. A complete file dump — sent anonymously to the international crime task force. Let justice trace the lines they burned.

scene6_screen3.text: They don’t stay. They don’t wait for headlines or handcuffs. But they know the story’s ending is already in motion.

scene6_screen4.text: They move without rush, without shadow. Just two travelers with no luggage and no return address.

scene6_screen6.text: (smirking) Now we see what hotel fate puts us in next. Maybe this time the keycard opens the right room.

scene6_screen7.text: (mockingly) Or the wrong one — with the right person.

scene6_screen8.text: She nudges him with her shoulder. He glances sideways — not quite smiling, but close.

scene6_screen9.text: There’s a flight to Lisbon in twenty. Or a coffee shop at Gate 14. Your call.

scene6_screen10.text: She raises an eyebrow — amused, undecided. Then with a quiet smile:

scene6_screen11.text: (teasing) I didn’t have a plan anyway. You’re just in time to be it.

scene6_screen12.text: He laughs — a real one this time. And when she nods, it’s not just agreement. It’s yes. To the moment. To the maybe.

scene6_screen13.text: They don’t promise forever. They don’t even promise tomorrow. But they walk through the gate — together.

scene6_screen14.text: Room 313 wasn’t just a number. It was a question: What would you do — when fate opens the wrong door?
